answer:
Let the five pitches be
\[
(6,b,c,d,6)
\]
with all entries positive integers and at most \(12\).

The three interior equalities are:
\[
\begin{aligned}
b&=|6-c| &&\text{(bell 2)},\\
c&=|b-d| &&\text{(bell 3)},\\
d&=|c-6| &&\text{(bell 4)}.
\end{aligned}
\]

From the first and third equalities,
\[
b=|6-c|=|c-6|=d,
\]
so \(b=d\).

Now substitute \(b=d\) into the middle equality:
\[
c=|b-d|=|b-b|=0.
\]
This contradicts the requirement that every pitch is a positive integer.

Therefore no row of five positive-integer pitches can satisfy all three interior equalities when the first and last pitches are both \(6\).

\[
\boxed{\text{No feasible rows exist.}}
\]

The bound “at most \(12\)” is irrelevant here; the contradiction occurs for all positive integer pitches.
